assignments.reason: מִשָּׁלוֹם ('from peace') is essentially שָׁלוֹם in its source-form. The Torah states 'עִקַּר הַדִּבּוּר הוּא מִשָּׁלוֹם' — the essential nature of this node is peace/shalom, the same domain as Package 1's core cluster of speech, peace, and warmth. It is a holy, positive concept: the source of all speech.

אַהֲבָה וְשָׁלוֹם ('love and peace') is essentially a compound of love and shalom — both are warm, connective, holy forces. The Torah presents love and peace as the spiritual state that enables speech and prayer. Its essential nature is peace (שָׁלוֹם) enriched by love (אַהֲבָה), placing it squarely in Package 1's domain of warm, connected, flowing holiness.

יוּכַל לְדַבֵּר בַּתְּפִלָּה ('able to speak in prayer') is essentially the actualized form of דִּבּוּר — speech in its highest expression (prayer). The Torah treats speech and prayer as one domain ('לְדַבֵּר וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל' are equated). Its essential nature is holy speech/prayer, the same domain as Package 1's central concept of דִּבּוּר.
